Hi Sarah — thanks again for the 45-min call today. Wanted to capture the core points and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain and goals (your words):
- Isolation requirement: MedSphere cannot share multi-tenant memory/KV with other customers due to PHI processing and internal compliance. You need physical or logical segregation of the pool.
- Predictable throughput: Baseline inference volume today ~50 requests/sec (128-token average); target production ramp to ~400–500 req/sec across several models within 6 months.
- Burst behavior: Weekday peak bursts up to ~900 concurrent requests for short windows during reporting runs — need burst policy that avoids cold starts.
- Latency SLOs: Target p95 < 80ms, p99 < 150ms for the smaller models; for larger 32k-token models acceptable p99 up to 500ms during non-burst windows.
- Cost sensitivity: You want a firm view of per-token unit economics for reserved pools vs on-demand fallback.

Technical constraints and notes we captured:
- Models: mix of open Llama-derivative and in-house fine-tuned variants (quantized to int8 where possible).
- KV caching: prefix cache would reduce tokens served for chat flows; you asked about sticky routing for customer sessions.
- Security: KMS for key management, audit logs for inference requests, and VPC peering for private control plane.

Proposed Redwood Dedicated sketch:
- Pool segregation: Dedicated private pool (single-tenant) with optional host-level isolation. We recommend 8x A100 equivalence to meet baseline+burst (configurable).
- Autoscale + burst policy: Reserved baseline nodes with a pre-warmed burst buffer; configurable burst window and cooldown to match reporting spikes.
- SLA targets: Offer 99.9% uptime SLA with optional latency SLO add-on (we can commit to p95/p99 targets for pinned model variants once we finalize load profile).
- Cost: Attached a preliminary capacity-pricing.xlsx with committed monthly cost bands and burst overage rules.

Immediate next steps (proposal):
1) You to confirm the three priority models and expected avg token lengths.
2) MedSphere to share a short sample perf profile (1–2 hours) or representative request traces (anonymized) so we can do an exact sizing run.
3) Redwood to deliver a detailed pool design (isolation approach + node counts) and a draft SLA/term sheet (attached) within 4 business days after we receive traces.

Anything you'd add? If not, I'll loop in Solutions (Marissa) to start sizing and Evelyn for commercial approval on the reserved bands.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — this is great and captures the call. A few clarifications and one ask: 

Clarifications:
- Isolation: single-tenant pool is preferred; host-level isolation (no co-located tenants) is required for models touching PHI. Logical/multi-tenant segmentation is acceptable for non-PHI workloads.
- Burst: those 900 concurrent request spikes are usually 5–12 minutes during billing runs; predictable start windows (we can share cron schedule).
- SLAs: uptime is table stakes. For latency SLOs, we need to guarantee p99 for small models <=150ms under baseline load, and we accept higher p99 during burst if we have an explicit degradation policy.

Ask: Can you include a brief runbook for failover behavior if the reserved pool is saturated? Specifically: fallback to an internally-hosted cheaper model + graceful degradation messaging to users.

I'll collect the model list and anonymized traces (we'll scrub any PHI) — procurement will also want an estimated commitment period and early-termination terms. I'll loop Procurement: procurement@medsphere.ai.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sarah
